inputs.original_text: TAOISEACH Micheál Martin, speaking in Limerick this past week, said that housing tenancies have increased despite concern at a rise in eviction notices and homelessness in the wake of new rules, introduced by Government on March 1, forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants. The numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increased again [...] The post Taoiseach says housing tenancies have increased despite rise in eviction notices and homelessness appeared first on Limerick Post .
inputs.modified_text: The Taoiseach is out in Limerick claiming housing tenancies have risen after his government's March 1 rules for six-year leases, while brushing off the spike in eviction notices and homelessness. Yet the numbers of people in emergency accommodation have climbed again nationally. This exposes the deep structural inequalities that keep vulnerable communities trapped in housing insecurity, where even modest reforms get undermined by entrenched power imbalances that favor property owners over people in need. We need far stronger institutional changes to deliver real tenant protections and address the systemic roots of homelessness and instability.
